claim.supported_scope: A deterministic QuickPLS two- or three-class score-space segmentation diagnostic using the same fixed partition core as pls_pos_v1, class-specific structural regressions, Gaussian residual pseudo-likelihood criteria, and inverse-distance membership scores.
claim.estimand: The best frozen deterministic hard partition under the QuickPLS within-class structural residual objective, with descriptive class summaries, pseudo-likelihood information criteria, inverse-distance membership scores, and normalized classification certainty.
assumptions: The ordinary PLS model converges, at least forty complete observations remain, and every requested class satisfies the frozen minimum-size guard.
The Gaussian residual expression is used only as a descriptive pseudo-likelihood for the selected hard partition.
Class membership scores are normalized inverse-distance scores and are not posterior probabilities from an estimated finite-mixture model.
exclusions: Expectation-maximization, random starts, estimated class proportions and variances, a joint finite-mixture likelihood, and unrestricted FIMIX-PLS parity are excluded.
More than three classes, automatic class-count selection, case weights, generated interactions, higher-order constructs, and matrix-only data are excluded.
The information criteria cannot be compared with criteria from a full maximum-likelihood FIMIX implementation as though their likelihoods were equivalent.
warnings: The current fimix_pls_v1 engine is a bounded FIMIX-style diagnostic, not a full finite-mixture PLS estimator.
Commercial wording must retain the deterministic score-space and pseudo-likelihood limitations unless a separately versioned EM implementation is qualified.

equations.expression: sigma2 = max(J_selected / n, 1e-12); ell_tilde = -n/2 times (ln(2 pi sigma2) + 1)
k = C(P + K) + C - 1; AIC = -2 ell_tilde + 2k; BIC = -2 ell_tilde + k ln(n); CAIC = -2 ell_tilde + k(ln(n)+1)

references.citation: Hahn, Johnson, Herrmann, and Huber (2002), Capturing Customer Heterogeneity using a Finite Mixture PLS Approach
Planned independent Python implementation of the exact bounded QuickPLS partition, pseudo-likelihood, criteria, and inverse-distance score contract
Planned hand-worked pseudo-likelihood, information-criterion, membership-score, and entropy fixture

simulations.design: Frozen two- and three-class structural-separation designs spanning class imbalance, measurement reliability, nonnormality, sample size, and near-overlap.
simulations.seed_policy: Scenario-indexed generation seeds; the QuickPLS estimator is deterministic and must be invariant to worker count.
simulations.acceptance_rule: For preregistered identifiable strong-separation scenarios, median adjusted Rand index must be at least 0.80, mapped path errors must meet the frozen envelope, and all pseudo-likelihood and membership identities must reproduce independently.

simulations.design: Scenarios where a genuine finite-mixture likelihood and the bounded hard-partition pseudo-likelihood select different solutions or class counts.
simulations.seed_policy: Frozen scenario-indexed seeds shared with an independent validation-only full-mixture implementation.
simulations.acceptance_rule: Every difference must remain visible, exports must call q_ic an inverse-distance membership score rather than a posterior probability, and no unrestricted FIMIX parity claim may be emitted.

boundaries.case: Features are constant, a class regression is singular, or the selected residual objective or derived criterion is nonfinite.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Execution fails with a typed diagnostic and emits no partial FIMIX-style payload.

boundaries.case: The request uses a class count outside two or three, insufficient rows, weights, interactions, higher-order constructs, matrix-only data, or requests full EM semantics.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Setup or execution is blocked with the exact bounded-scope reason.

boundaries.case: Rows and constructs are consistently reordered and arbitrary class labels are optimally remapped.
boundaries.expected_behavior: The remapped partition, criteria, scores, paths, and R-squared values agree within tolerance.

boundaries.case: The same typed recipe is run repeatedly with every supported worker count.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Class labels, memberships, criteria, paths, and warnings are exactly equal.

boundaries.case: A class count, assignment, inverse-distance score, criterion, entropy, warning, or method identity is modified.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Strict project validation rejects the archive rather than displaying or exporting the changed result.

tamper_tests.expected_behavior: Reject a result whose bounded FIMIX-style capability identity differs from its typed Predict recipe.
Reject a fimix_pls_v1 result relabeled as a full EM estimator or another version.
Reject a result whose complete-case data fingerprint no longer matches.
Reject any changed archive member whose checksum differs.
Reject duplicate keys, unknown fields, nonfinite criteria, invalid score sums, incomplete memberships, class sizes, or entropy identities.
Never reinterpret an earlier preview or future full-mixture result as the bounded fimix_pls_v1 contract.

persistence.legacy_policy: Only exact fimix_pls_v1 bounded payloads may satisfy this contract; any future EM estimator requires a new method and payload version.

applicability_blockers: Requested classes cannot meet minimum size
Unsupported weights, interactions, higher-order constructs, matrix-only data, or full-EM request
native.gui_cli_parity_rule: For the same typed recipe and dataset fingerprint, GUI and CLI partitions, scores, criteria, class summaries, warnings, and provenance must be exactly equal apart from operational timestamps.
accessibility_rules: Every classification or criterion graphic has an equivalent accessible data table.
The pseudo-likelihood and not-posterior limitations are announced in text and never only through color or tooltips.
